claims.text: In our uncalibrated relative phone-audio recordings in the passenger saloon, mean levels on the Central line were -18.66 dBFS(A) eastbound on LST-BTH (n=6, sd=0.35), -19.42 dBFS(A) eastbound on BTH-MLE (n=6, sd=0.35), -18.8 dBFS(A) westbound on BTH-LST (n=5, sd=0.48), and -19.07 dBFS(A) westbound on MLE-BTH (n=5, sd=0.65).

Across 11 placement-ok trips, the mean within-trip relative difference between LST-BTH and BTH-MLE was 0.54 dB (sd 0.36, range -0.13 to 1.21, positive in 10 of 11 trips, one-sided sign test p=0.0059), which resulted in a pre-registered NO-GO verdict because the contrast is below 1 dB and inside phone limiter compression and run-to-run variation.

Our uncalibrated relative levels on both Central line sections (-18.66 to -19.42 dBFS(A)) were substantially higher than on the sub-surface parallel route between Liverpool Street, Aldgate East, and Whitechapel (-22.67 dBFS(A) on EB LST-ALE, -25.52 dBFS(A) on EB ALE-WCL, -24.54 dBFS(A) on WB WCL-ALE, and -24.65 dBFS(A) on WB ALE-LST) and quieter Central line sections such as EB HOL-CYL (-23.51 dBFS(A)).

Separate indicative measurements using the NIOSH Sound Level Meter app on an iPhone in the passenger saloon over one whole trip per direction between Liverpool Street and Mile End (including platform waits and the Bethnal Green dwell) recorded 91.9 dB(A) LAeq eastbound (max 109.7 dB, LCpeak 124.4 dB) and 87.3 dB(A) LAeq westbound (max 105.3 dB, LCpeak 120.2 dB), though the app is validated only up to about 85 dB(A) so readings above that may read low and cannot be compared like-for-like with TfL's per-section in-cab figures.

Under The Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 cited in TfL's acoustic reports (Weir-letter-2022-12), the workplace lower exposure action value for workers is a daily personal noise exposure level (LEP,d) of 80 dB(A), the upper exposure action value is 85 dB(A), and the exposure limit value is 87 dB(A).

claims.text: The 92.8 decibels figure for Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green appears only in a secondary press article (Brixton Buzz, 27 January 2026, attributing the study to JRPass) without specifying the underlying TfL document, measurement date, direction, or whether it was recorded in the cab or passenger saloon.

citations.quote: Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green (Central line) – 92.8 decibels
Daniel de Nieuwe, Head of Product from JRPass said:

claims.text: Because Mayor's Question 2022/1791 does not specify which track direction or chainage was ground between December 2021 and May 2022, and because no post-2022 Central line grinding logs or pre-2024 section-by-section noise readings are in the public corpus, the evidence cannot establish whether LST-BTH or BTH-MLE were ground again after May 2022, whether the planned 2023/24 eastbound deep Tube reconditioning on LST-BTH was completed, or how noise levels changed immediately before and after grinding.

asks.request: Provide the complete log of all rail grinding works carried out on the Central line between Liverpool Street, Bethnal Green, and Mile End from January 2021 to the present, specifying for each intervention the date, track direction (eastbound/westbound), and start and end chainage (metres).
asks.why: MQ 2022/1791 confirms grinding took place between December 2021 and May 2022 on both sections, and TfL states grinding must be repeated every 6 to 12 months, but the public record does not state which direction was ground or whether any grinding has occurred in the years since (C1, C4, C15).

asks.request: Confirm whether the Deep Tube Reconditioning works planned for financial year 2023/24 on Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green Eastbound (converting Pandrol Vanguard to Delkor fastenings) were completed, including the completion date and chainage covered, and whether any reconditioning is planned for the westbound track or for Bethnal Green to Mile End.
asks.why: TfL's Head of Track listed Liverpool Street - Bethnal Green Eastbound in the 2023/24 reconditioning plan in December 2022, and later updates note 7 completed and 9 in-progress sites across the network without identifying if this Central line section was among them (C3, C15).

asks.request: Release all bi-monthly in-cab noise measurements (dB LAeq and LCpeak, eastbound and westbound) recorded on the Central line from January 2021 to the present, together with any passenger saloon noise measurements and the specific dataset or FOI response underlying the 92.8 dB figure for Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green cited in the press.
asks.why: TfL confirmed in FOI-1231-2425 that Central line readings are carried out bi-monthly and that June 2024 cab levels were 86-87 dB LAeq on LST-BTH and 82-83 dB LAeq on BTH-MLE, but without the bi-monthly time series it is impossible to evaluate the effectiveness and decay rate of grinding or verify the 92.8 dB secondary press figure (C5, C6, C13, C14, C15).

asks.request: Provide the latest rail roughness (corrugation) plots for both eastbound and westbound tracks between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green and between Bethnal Green and Mile End.
asks.why: TfL previously disclosed rail roughness plots for Bethnal Green to Mile End under FOI-1730-1819 in 2018 and states that it uses a data-led approach analysing network-wide corrugation to prioritise grinding, yet refuses to share section-level data with Assembly Members (C2, C13).

asks.why: TfL confirmed in FOI-1231-2425 that Central line readings are carried out bi-monthly and that June 2024 cab levels were 86-87 dB LAeq on LST-BTH and 82-83 dB LAeq on BTH-MLE, but without the bi-monthly time series it is impossible to evaluate the effectiveness and decay rate of grinding or verify the 92.8 dB secondary press figure (C5, C6, C13, C14, C15).

asks.request: Provide the latest rail roughness (corrugation) plots for both eastbound and westbound tracks between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green and between Bethnal Green and Mile End.
asks.why: TfL previously disclosed rail roughness plots for Bethnal Green to Mile End under FOI-1730-1819 in 2018 and states that it uses a data-led approach analysing network-wide corrugation to prioritise grinding, yet refuses to share section-level data with Assembly Members (C2, C13).
